history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN (flag): the CSV row 'Venu Gopala Swamy Temple, Rajahmundry' matches more than one referent. (a) The historic Venu Gopala Swamy of Rajahmundry was the kshetra palaka (court deity) of the Chalukya kings, for whom Raja Raja Narendra is said to have built a temple on Swethagiri hill inside his 11th-century fort; researchers note the present Royal Mosque on Rajahmundry's main road retains Hindu temple features and may stand on that temple's site. (b) A modern Venugopala Swamy Temple exists in Rajahmundry city (geocoded at Rajahmundry Main Road, Sambhu Nagar/Alcot Gardens; also listed at railway gate street/Pedda Veedhi). This file is provisionally mapped to (b); treat all details below as needing verification against the intended temple. Coordinates are from the map geocoder POI match, not from a web source.

town_description: Rajahmundry, on the east bank of the Godavari in East Godavari district, is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Andhra Pradesh. Founded in the 11th century by the Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra, it is called the cultural capital of Andhra, noted for its Telugu literary heritage, Pushkar ghats and temples.
